title: Prove one-scale zero-swap helper-462 words need at least 9 shears.
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->

## Change and mathematical scope

Proof. No new κ. The selected record stays `781451/250000000`.

Under the zero-swap, one-scale hypotheses of open PR #7030, every rational elementary word for the pinned helper-462 matcher has at least **9** shears. Subadditivity of `rank(W - I)` still gives only 8, and that rank is 8 on the matrix, so the stronger bound is not the same invariant. The new invariant is the elementary rank-drop depth. On the recorded 29-shear word it equals 2. The same exhaustive census on every scale row has depth at most 2, so a factorization into 8 elementary shears does not exist.

The #7030 recorded 29-shear word still multiplies to the matcher, but it is not the shortest known one-scale word. Sibling unpaidmoon fork draft [PR 234](https://github.com/unpaidmoon/integer-mult-bounds/pull/234) (r195, `research/helper462-one-scale-26-shear`, head `ae1cf2af174cd4f8c89089a27fc58e470b5452bd`) records a constructive 26-shear one-scale zero-swap word. Twenty-six is not claimed to be minimal. Nine is not shown to be sharp. Lengths 9 through 25 stay open. This census is finite only because each rank-dropping edge has at most one coefficient. It is not a census of words that contain a non-dropping shear.

No supplier admission, no P2 ordinary bill, and no integer-coefficient claim. The integer obstruction remains the theorem of #6954.

## Task and overlap

Base: `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`, priority revision 8. The verifier reads `certificates/selected-result.json`; `current-priorities.md` on this base still quotes the older selected value from #5599.

Task card: `supplier-boundary-audit`, scope **refined**. The question is open question 2 of open PR #7030: whether the rank lower bound of 8 can be raised under the same hypotheses. The requested first step was to name a different invariant and evaluate it on the recorded 29-shear word.

Nearest work, and why this is distinct:

- Open #7030 records the 29-shear word and the rank lower bound of 8, and leaves this question open. The word is copied from commit `98238eeed3faca9f0a5f1d4060db5d5da524a192` and rechecked against the pinned matcher. Open question 1 of #7030 (a shorter one-scale word) is not proved in this package; sibling fork draft PR 234 records a 26-shear constructive witness for that question, not a minimum.
- Merged #6954 records a one-scale word of length 53 and the determinant identity used to move the scale.
- Open #7012 records a 25-shear word with eleven scales. That is not a one-scale length.
- The odd-denominator bound for the landing permutation is a different matrix and a different coefficient ring.

Package: `research/helper462-one-scale-rank-drop`.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only, from the repository root:

```sh
python3 -B research/helper462-one-scale-rank-drop/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/helper462-one-scale-rank-drop/verify.py
python3 -O -B research/helper462-one-scale-rank-drop/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/helper462-one-scale-rank-drop
```

Proof controls use an explicit failure function, so they stay active under `-O`. Expected token: `PASS_HELPER462_ONE_SCALE_RANK_DROP`.

Checked here: selected κ is unchanged; the published 24 right-route factors multiply to `S`; the recorded word multiplies to `S`; moving its scale and returning it preserves 29 shears and the product; mutating the scale, the first shear, or dropping the first shear misses `S`; one shear has rank distance 1; an explicit 8-shear matrix in `SL(8)` peels back to `I`; `diag(2, 1/2)` has rank distance 2 and depth 0; for every scale row the minor test and the pairing test agree on every edge, the depth is the pinned value at most 2, and the tree does not reach `I`.

No Lean, Docker, or selected cold replay was run.

## Credit

The matcher and the 24 right-route factors are from `research/bit-completed-backend-api` (Chris R / Clear1nsight, PR #4957), using the helper-462 witness of ai-nanachi #4760/#4814. The determinant identity and the balanced-scale identity are PR #6954. The recorded 29-shear word, the scale-moving lemma, and the rank lower bound of 8 are PR #7030. The 26-shear one-scale witness cited above is sibling fork draft PR 234 and is not part of this package. Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Can the elementary shear lower bound be raised above 9 under the same hypotheses? A word of length 9 has one shear that does not drop `rank(· - I)`, and that coefficient is not fixed by the rank-drop equation, so the same census does not decide it. The useful first step is to name an invariant that charges one non-dropping shear and evaluate it on this same recorded word. An explicit one-scale word of length 26 is recorded in sibling fork draft PR 234; lengths 9 through 25 remain open. That shorter-word search is not taken here.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

Requiring the minor test and the pairing test to agree made a false rejection of a legal edge fail the run, instead of turning into a spurious lower bound.
